newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains cattle market slow Wednesday- feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains cattle market slow Wednesday- feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were slow Wednesday amid light sales of off-quality cattle, with the bulk of this week's showlist still waiting for buyers, feedlot sources said.
Packers bid $71.00 per cwt, with owners asking mostly $73.00 for their cattle.
About 800 head traded in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area and about 400 in Kansas at $71.00, but below average market grades, the sources said.
Most feedlot sources expect cattle to trade by Thursday at $73.00, unchanged from last week's top.
Prices were expected to be supported by tight numbers of finished cattle, feedlot sources said.

However, prices could be pressured by continued weakness in beef prices, which were eroding packer operating margins, market sources said. Midday beef prices were quoted down $0.15 to $0.68 per cwt, according to USDA.
Wednesday's decline in CME live cattle futures also could weigh on fed cattle prices Thursday, market sources said.
